wellopti.options.title: WellOpti Settings
wellopti.options.disableWhileScoping.too: Draw everything at full distance while you're looking through a spyglass.
wellopti.options.dynamicFps.enabled.tool: Lower the frame rate when you aren't looking at the game, so your GPU, fans and battery get a break.
wellopti.options.dynamicFps.unfocused.to: FPS cap while another window has focus, for example when you alt-tab.
wellopti.options.dynamicFps.minimized.to: FPS cap while the game window is minimised. Vanilla uses 10.
wellopti.options.dynamicFps.paused.toolt: FPS cap while a singleplayer game is paused.
wellopti.options.entityCulling.enabled.t: Skip drawing entities and mobs that are far away. Glowing entities, bosses and players are always drawn.
wellopti.options.entityCulling.droppedIt: Distance past which dropped items aren't drawn.
wellopti.options.entityCulling.experienc: Distance past which experience orbs aren't drawn.
wellopti.options.entityCulling.itemFrame: Distance past which item frames, and the maps and items in them, aren't drawn.
wellopti.options.entityCulling.armorStan: Distance past which armor stands aren't drawn.
wellopti.options.entityCulling.stuckArro: Distance past which arrows and tridents stuck in blocks aren't drawn. Arrows in flight are always drawn.
wellopti.options.entityCulling.ambientMo: Distance past which bats, fish, tadpoles and squid aren't drawn.
wellopti.options.blockEntityCulling.enab: Skip drawing detailed blocks that are far away. Vanilla draws these out to 64 blocks.
wellopti.options.blockEntityCulling.sign: Distance past which text on signs isn't drawn. The sign itself stays visible.
wellopti.options.blockEntityCulling.bann: Distance past which banners aren't drawn.
wellopti.options.blockEntityCulling.skul: Distance past which mob and player heads aren't drawn.
wellopti.options.blockEntityCulling.stor: Distance past which chests, ender chests and shulker boxes aren't drawn.
wellopti.options.blockEntityCulling.item: Distance past which items on shelves and campfires, and decorated pots, aren't drawn.
wellopti.options.particles.enabled.toolt: Limit how many particles can exist at once, so explosions and particle spam can't tank your FPS.
wellopti.options.particles.max.tooltip: The most particles allowed at once. Item pickup animations always get through.
wellopti.preset.quality.tooltip: Light touch. Culls only at long range, so you'll barely notice anything missing.
wellopti.preset.balanced.tooltip: The defaults. A good boost with distances most people won't notice.
wellopti.preset.performance.tooltip: Shorter distances, fewer particles, lower background FPS. For weaker PCs and busy bases.
wellopti.preset.potato.tooltip: Anything for frames. Things will pop in close to you, but your toaster will thank you.
wellopti.options.occlusionCulling.enable: Skip drawing mobs, items, chests and other detailed objects that are completely hidden behind solid blocks. The biggest win in caves, bases and around farms.
wellopti.options.occlusionCulling.entiti: Hide mobs, items and other entities behind walls. Players are never hidden, because their name tags show through walls.
wellopti.options.occlusionCulling.blockE: Hide chests, signs, banners, heads and similar blocks behind walls.
wellopti.options.backgroundAudio.unfocus: Game volume while you're in another window. 100%% leaves it alone.
wellopti.options.backgroundAudio.minimiz: Game volume while the window is minimised. 100%% leaves it alone; 0%% mutes it.
wellopti.options.hud.enabled.tooltip: A small overlay with your FPS, memory use, and how much WellOpti is skipping. Hidden while F3 is open.
wellopti.options.hud.corner.tooltip: Which corner of the screen the HUD sits in.
wellopti.options.hud.showMemory.tooltip: Show how much of Java's memory the game is using.
wellopti.options.hud.showCulling.tooltip: Show how many things WellOpti skipped drawing each frame.
wellopti.options.entityCulling.passiveMo: Distance past which cows, sheep, pigs, chickens, horses and other animals aren't drawn. Named mobs are always drawn.
wellopti.options.entityCulling.villagers: Distance past which villagers and wandering traders aren't drawn. Named villagers are always drawn.
wellopti.options.entityCulling.hostileMo: Distance past which zombies, skeletons, creepers and other monsters aren't drawn. Bosses and named mobs are always drawn. Vanilla stops drawing most of these at about 64-70 blocks anyway.
Past this distance, mobs skip drawing armor, held items, elytra, heads and saddles. Body details like sheep wool and villager outfits always draw, and so does players' gear.
wellopti.options.mobs.nameTagDistance.to: Past this distance, name tags on mobs aren't drawn. Vanilla uses 64 blocks. Players' name tags are left alone.
wellopti.options.mobs.crowdLimit.tooltip: Draw at most this many mobs in the same block. Mob farms cram dozens of animals into one block, where you can't tell 8 from 80. The rest are still there, just not drawn.
wellopti.options.blockEntityCulling.spaw: Distance past which monster spawners (and the little spinning mob inside), trial spawners and vaults aren't drawn.
wellopti.options.adaptive.enabled.toolti: When your FPS drops below the target, gradually shrink all culling distances; grow them back once it recovers. Great for busy areas that only lag sometimes.
wellopti.options.adaptive.targetFps.tool: The frame rate adaptive mode tries to keep. If your Max Framerate setting is lower, that's used instead. With VSync on, set this at or below your monitor's refresh rate.
wellopti.options.adaptive.minScale.toolt: The furthest distances can shrink, as a percentage of their normal value.
wellopti.options.benchmark.tooltip: Closes this screen and measures your FPS for 15 seconds with WellOpti on, then 15 seconds with it off, in the same spot. Stand still somewhere busy and don't open menus.
wellopti.options.benchmark.needWorld: Join a world first: the benchmark measures FPS in-game.
wellopti.benchmark.started: WellOpti benchmark starting. Stand still, look at something busy, and don't open any menus. Takes about 30 seconds.
wellopti.benchmark.resultOn: With WellOpti: %s FPS average, %s FPS 1%% low
wellopti.benchmark.resultOff: Without WellOpti: %s FPS average, %s FPS 1%% low
wellopti.benchmark.difference: Difference: %s average FPS, %s 1%% low (the 1%% low is the slowest frames, i.e. stutter)
wellopti.benchmark.alreadyRunning: A benchmark is already running. /wellopti benchmark stop cancels it.
wellopti.benchmark.needWorld: Join a world first: the benchmark measures FPS in-game.
wellopti.benchmark.noToggle: Can't toggle WellOpti while a benchmark is running
wellopti.benchmark.cancelled.leftWorld: Benchmark cancelled: you left the world.
wellopti.benchmark.cancelled.menu: Benchmark cancelled: a menu opened or the window lost focus, which changes FPS on purpose. Try again and leave the game in front.
wellopti.options.particles.ambientDistan: Decorative particles (campfire smoke, rain splashes, drips, spores, falling leaves, ash, bubble columns, fireflies) aren't spawned further away than this. Particles that tell you something are never affected.
wellopti.options.particles.ambientDensit: How many decorative particles spawn at all. 100%% is vanilla.
wellopti.options.memoryAdvisor.tooltip: Show a short notice if Minecraft was given very little memory, or if memory stays nearly full for a while.
wellopti.memory.low.title: Minecraft is low on memory
wellopti.memory.low.message: Only %s MB is allocated. Set it to 4 GB in your launcher's Java settings for smoother play.
wellopti.memory.full.title: Memory is nearly full
wellopti.memory.full.message: Minecraft has been using over 90%% of its %s MB for a while. Allocating more in your launcher can stop stutters.
wellopti.options.entityCulling.paintings: Distance past which paintings aren't drawn.
Distance past which empty minecarts and boats aren't drawn. Storage systems and hopper-minecart farms can have hundreds. Ones with someone riding are always drawn.
wellopti.options.entityCulling.throttleH: Entities WellOpti isn't drawing (behind walls, too far away, or over a farm's crowd limit) update 5 times a second on your screen instead of 20. They catch up the moment they're visible again. The server still runs every mob normally, so farms and gameplay don't change. Players, anything being ridden and nearby entities always update normally.
wellopti.options.perServerPresets.toolti: When you pick a preset while playing, WellOpti remembers it for that server (singleplayer counts as one) and switches back to it whenever you join there again.
wellopti.preset.restored: WellOpti: using the %s preset for this server
